cause: The first CA oracle fixture had repeated singular values, so R and NumPy selected different valid bases for the same singular subspace.

impact.initial_failure: coordinate comparison failed despite equal singular values
impact.resolution: the oracle now uses a non-degenerate fixed table and permits only per-axis SVD sign flips

lesson: External SVD oracles must avoid repeated singular values or compare invariant subspaces rather than arbitrary basis vectors.

cause: The corrected MI and Rubin contracts intentionally fail before production implementation.

expected_failures: m=1 single_imputation mode is not yet emitted
Rubin pool API is not yet implemented

lesson: Keep the corrected statistical and lineage contract red until production behavior satisfies it.

cause: The shared replicate-and-combine foundation was implemented after the red contract and passed focused verification.
lesson: Keep replicate generation, adapter evidence, and statistical combination as named typed contracts with bounded aggregate provenance.

cause: The missingness and Rubin contracts were intentionally red before production implementation.
lesson: Keep the descriptive missingness and Rubin statistical contracts red until the production pack owns their validation and numerical semantics.

cause: The corrected MICE generation, lineage, Rubin pooling, and OLS consumer passed the focused and adjacent regression boundary after review removed first-imputation fit statistics.
lesson: A pooled MI result must not inherit fit statistics, residuals, covariance or inference configuration from the first imputation.

cause: The new Bootstrap, permutation, and resampling envelope tests were intentionally added before their production modules.

impact.result: 2 collection errors: production consumer modules were absent

lesson: Keep each resampling consumer red until its typed strategy, adapter, combiner, and safety boundary exist.

cause: The first R Oracle assertion compared 1e-14 against R's default six-digit console rendering, so correct values were truncated before comparison.

impact.result: 2 Oracle assertions failed before the fixed precision output

lesson: External numerical Oracles must fix their serialization precision before applying tight equality tolerances.

cause: The shared typed combiner, digest-bound resampling envelope, Bootstrap intervals, exact and Monte Carlo permutation inference, and external R Oracle checks passed together.
lesson: Resampling consumers must share bounded provenance execution while keeping Rubin, bootstrap interval, permutation p-value, and survey covariance mathematics as separate named combiners.

cause: The explicit GMM and weak-instrument contracts were added before their production pack existed.

impact.expected: typed IV/GMM envelope and weak-instrument diagnostics remain red until implemented
impact.result: 2 collection errors: GMM production modules were absent

lesson: Keep the GMM estimator and weak-instrument diagnostic boundary red until closed-form numerical semantics and fail-closed input validation exist.

cause: The first GMM run exposed a NumPy scalar boundary rejection, an incorrectly constructed underidentification fixture, and a reference mismatch between optimizer-based statsmodels IVGMM and the closed-form one-step estimator.

impact.resolution: accepted NumPy integer/floating scalars, corrected the underidentification fixture, and bound the one-step Oracle to statsmodels IV2SLS closed form

lesson: Numerical Oracles must compare like-for-like estimators; optimizer output is not a valid reference for a closed-form one-step GMM implementation.

cause: The explicit one-step/two-step GMM estimator, Hansen J evidence, and weak-instrument diagnostics passed the focused numerical and contract boundary after review.

impact.oracle: statsmodels IV2SLS closed-form one-step and IVGMM two-step checks passed

lesson: GMM must expose estimator, covariance, identification, Hansen, and weak-instrument semantics explicitly; it must not invent automatic Stock--Yogo threshold decisions.

cause: The first post-hoc verification exposed an over-broad raw-field assertion, an R Scheffe fixture using the wrong within-group denominator, a statsmodels studentized-range p-value floor, and a small inverse-CDF endpoint discrepancy.

impact.initial_result: 3 failures, then 1 endpoint-only failure after the first correction
impact.resolution: checked raw keys structurally, corrected Scheffe MSE to df_within, replaced the statsmodels p-value floor with bounded direct quadrature, and documented the q inverse tolerance

lesson: An external numerical Oracle must validate its own degrees-of-freedom algebra and serialization precision; library tail limits must be treated as a correctness boundary, not a harmless approximation.

cause: Scheffe and Games--Howell now publish digest-bound pairwise evidence with explicit distribution, degrees-of-freedom, confidence-interval, backend, and rejection semantics.

impact.safety: constant-variance groups, nonfinite values, bounds, raw payloads, and small-d.f. backend semantics are explicit

lesson: Post-hoc methods must remain separate named combiners: Scheffe uses pooled ANOVA MSE, while Games--Howell uses Welch degrees of freedom and a studentized-range tail.

cause: The new typed survey bridge was specified before its adapter module existed; the existing survey mathematics remained present but no new pack could consume it through the shared replicate boundary.

impact.boundary: survey/ design construction was intentionally not modified
impact.result: 1 collection error: survey_adapter module was absent

lesson: Add survey support at a typed adapter boundary so existing design mathematics can be reused without adding a family enumeration or editing the survey kernel.

cause: The typed survey bridge consumes existing jackknife, BRR, provided, and bootstrap weight builders through the shared replicate boundary without modifying survey design mathematics.

impact.oracle: R-generated jackknife and fixed-Hadamard BRR standard errors matched

lesson: Survey-aware expansion should add typed estimator adapters at the replicate boundary; it must not fork or edit the already-validated design, lonely-PSU, FPC, or replicate-weight mathematics.

cause: The first cross-pack pytest command placed the complete file list in one quoted shell variable expansion, so pytest received one nonexistent path instead of individual test arguments.

impact.resolution: reran with individual path arguments; 607 tests passed
impact.result: pytest exited 4 with no tests run

lesson: Keep bounded gate command paths as explicit arguments; a shell aggregation error must not be mistaken for a test result.

cause: The ordered P7 extension slices passed together after the survey adapter was added, with protected Claude paths, survey mathematics, runtime shell boundaries, and Python compilation checked separately.

evidence.ref: P7 standalone packs + MI/resampling/GMM/posthoc/survey regression suite

impact.runtime_safety_scan: no Rscript/subprocess/shell/eval/exec/import-path hits in new runtime modules

lesson: Keep each statistical capability as a standalone typed kernel first; integrate only after cross-pack numerical evidence, protected-path isolation, and fail-closed runtime scans pass together.

cause: A delegated implementation attempt wrote production files before the required red test; the files were removed and the task was restarted test first.
lesson: For delegated coding, require a failing test artifact before accepting any production patch; when the order is violated, remove the patch and restart from the red test.

cause: The first temporary formal event fixture used a malformed UUID and was rejected before it could be appended; the fixture was corrected and the intended failure event was appended.
lesson: Validate UUIDs and event shape locally before invoking the formal append command.

cause: The bounded P7 extension scope contract passed specification and code-quality review after closing-key, path-shape, prose, and repeated-backslash boundary fixes.
lesson: Represent P7 applicability and limitations as a bounded typed contract, and test both unsafe path/code shapes and safe statistical prose before pack implementation.

cause: Five independently dispatched P7 pack agents remained running across repeated bounded waits and returned no code, tests, or RED evidence; they were closed to prevent an unbounded wait.

impact.recovery: re-dispatch one bounded pack task at a time

lesson: Use bounded subagent tasks with an explicit checkpoint and recover to smaller sequential slices when parallel workers remain running without verifiable artifacts.

cause: The first hurdle GLM Oracle assertion compared the product of marginal gate and truncated means with the observation-wise mean of their product, conflating two distinct predictive estimands.

impact.production_result: corrected to preserve observation-wise unconditional mean

lesson: Keep conditional and marginal predictive estimands separate; a scalar identity that looks plausible must not replace the observation-wise estimand.

cause: The first base-R Synthetic Control fixture passed grad=NULL to constrOptim, so the external Oracle failed before evaluating the constrained optimum.

impact.oracle_fixture: corrected with an explicit numerical gradient

lesson: A constrained external Oracle must test the numerical reference itself before it can validate the production estimator; fixture optimizer arguments are part of the evidence boundary.

cause: A temporary formal event fixture used an underscore in lesson_key, while the devline event schema accepts normalized hyphenated identifiers only; append was rejected before changing the event chain.

impact.recovery: lesson_key normalized and the intended event was appended

lesson: Validate event identifiers against the formal schema before invoking append; a rejected temporary fixture must be corrected without bypassing the controlled writer.

cause: The six final standalone P7 packs were reviewed against their closed contracts, scope metadata, failure semantics, Oracle boundaries, and protected-path rules.

impact.known_limits: documented in findings and freeze handoff

lesson: A statistical kernel is ready for adoption only when its numerical output, estimand labels, unsupported extensions, and integration boundary are reviewed together.

cause: The final P7 extension slice completed its focused numerical, external Oracle, compilation, runtime-safety, protected-path, whitespace, and formal-line checks.

impact.external_oracles: base-R/direct-formula and statsmodels checks passed where available
impact.release_boundary: full gate, Agent/browser E2E, merge, push, tag, and release deferred

lesson: Freeze a statistical kernel only with numerical evidence and an explicit integration boundary; deferred reachability and release checks must remain visible rather than being implied by unit-test green.

cause: The complete set of P7/MI/survey/resampling tests changed since the d032958 baseline was rerun after the final extension implementation and freeze documentation.

impact.release_boundary: this does not execute the deferred full release gate or Agent/browser E2E

lesson: Run the affected historical regression after the final slice, and distinguish its backend evidence from the later integration and release gates.
